stem: A purified bacterial capsular polysaccharide vaccine produces an inadequate response in a target pediatric population. A redesigned vaccine chemically links the same polysaccharide to a protein carrier. Which of the following is the principal purpose of adding the carrier?

options.label: A
options.misconception: Confuses an antigen-containing vaccine with passive immunoglobulin therapy.
options.explanation: A conjugate vaccine stimulates the recipient's immune response rather than supplying ready-made antibody.

options.label: B
options.text: Prevent antigen uptake by B lymphocytes
options.misconception: Mistakes the carrier for a barrier to antigen recognition rather than a way to change the response.
options.explanation: Protein conjugation does not work by preventing B lymphocytes from encountering the polysaccharide antigen.

options.label: C
options.misconception: Correctly identifies the immune-response change produced by covalent protein conjugation.
options.explanation: Adding the carrier changes polysaccharide immunity from a T-cell-independent pattern to a T-cell-dependent one, allowing more durable protection.

options.label: D
options.text: Restrict antigen recognition to CD8 cells
options.misconception: Confuses T-cell dependence with an isolated cytotoxic T-cell response.
options.explanation: The purpose is not to restrict recognition to CD8 cells but to make the polysaccharide response T-cell dependent.

options.label: E
options.text: Permit replication of the vaccine organism
options.misconception: Mistakes a nonliving conjugate product for a live attenuated vaccine.
options.explanation: Chemical linkage does not create a viable organism or confer the ability to reproduce in the recipient.

context:
Learning objective: distinguish T-cell-independent polysaccharide responses from T-cell-dependent conjugate vaccine responses.

Covalently linking a bacterial polysaccharide to a carrier protein converts the response to T-cell dependence and thereby supports longer-term immunity.
